ELECTION
Scope:
These rules shall apply to this contract.
Underlying:
The Underlying for this Contract is the official results of <election> as reported by the Source Agencies. The

Underlying specifically refers to: (i) for direct democratic elections, the candidate/party declared elected by the relevant

electoral authority; (ii) for parliamentary/legislative elections, the party, coalition, or alliance winning the most seats in the

specified chamber; (iii) for indirect elections by electoral bodies, the candidate elected through the prescribed process; (iv)

for religious/ecclesiastical elections, the individual selected through the prescribed religious process and confirmed by

religious authorities; (v) for traditional/customary leadership selections, the individual recognized through both traditional

processes and relevant governmental authorities where applicable; (vi) for judicial elections/retentions, the candidate elected

or retained per the specified system; (vii) for recall elections, whether the official is recalled; (viii) for votes of no

confidence, whether the motion passes; (ix) for referenda/plebiscites/ballot measures, whether the proposal achieves the

required threshold; (x) for constituent assemblies, the party/coalition winning the most seats or the constitutional proposal's

approval; (xi) for professional/corporate governance elections, the individual selected through the prescribed process; (xii)

for hereditary positions with electoral components, the individual selected through the prescribed succession process; (xiii)

for rotational/consensual leadership systems, the individual/party designated for the specified period. Revisions to the

Underlying made after Expiration will not be accounted for in determining the Expiration Value.
Source Agency:
The Source Agencies are, in hierarchical order: (1) Primary Sources: the official electoral commission,

constitutional court, or equivalent electoral authority of the relevant jurisdiction; the formal proclamation by the head of state

or government when constitutionally required; for religious elections, the official religious authority (e.g., Vatican for papal

elections, relevant Patriarchate for Orthodox elections); for traditional leadership, both the traditional authority and relevant

government recognition body; for professional elections, the governing board or regulatory authority; (2) Secondary Sources:

for international elections, the United Nations Electoral Assistance Division, Organization of American States, African

Union, European Union Election Observation Missions, Commonwealth Secretariat, Carter Center, International IDEA,

International Foundation for Electoral Systems; (3) Tertiary Sources: major newspapers of record in the relevant jurisdiction

in order of circulation, Reuters, Associated Press, Bloomberg News, Agence France-Presse, The New York Times, Financial

Times, The Wall Street Journal, BBC, France24, Deutsche Welle, NHK World, Al Jazeera English, The Washington Post,

Axios, Politico, Semafor, The Information, ABC, CBS, CNN, Fox News, MSNBC, NBC.
Type:
The type of Contract is an Event Contract.
Issuance:
After the initial Contract, Contract iterations will be listed on an as-needed basis at the discretion of the Exchange

and corresponding to the risk management needs of Members.
<candidate/party/option>:
<candidate/party/option> refers to an individual candidate, political party, electoral

coalition/alliance (formal pre-election only), religious candidate, traditional candidate, judicial candidate, referendum option

(Yes/No/specific choices), recall target, confidence motion, or other electoral choice specified by the Exchange. For

coalitions/alliances, only those formally registered with electoral authorities before the nomination deadline count, not post-
election governing arrangements. For religious elections, includes all eligible candidates under religious law. For write-in

candidates, only those meeting legal requirements for ballot access. The Exchange may list iterations for "Other," "None of

the Above," "No Valid Election Held," "Election Postponed Beyond Expiration," "Blank/Null/Spoiled Votes," or

"Abstention" where relevant. In indirect elections, <candidate/party/option> refers to the ultimate officeholder, not

intermediate selectors.
<election>:
<election> refers to a specific electoral event specified by the Exchange, including: jurisdiction (international,

national, regional, state, provincial, municipal, religious, traditional, professional); type (presidential, parliamentary,

legislative, judicial, constituent assembly, referendum, plebiscite, recall, confidence vote, religious selection, traditional

selection, professional board); electoral system (first-past-the-post, proportional representation, mixed-member, ranked

choice, single transferable vote, approval, score/range, Condorcet, Borda count, cumulative, limited, single non-transferable

vote, consensual allocation, religious discernment, traditional selection); round (first round, runoff, final ballot); specific

[page 2 of 4: text layer]
position (for rotational systems); and date or year. For multi-stage elections, the Exchange will specify which stage. For

elections with multiple simultaneous components, each component constitutes a separate Contract unless specified otherwise.
<date>:
<date> refers to a calendar date specified by the Exchange. The Exchange may list iterations of the Contract

corresponding to variations of <date>. All times are in Eastern Time (ET) unless otherwise specified.
Payout Criterion:
The Payout Criterion for the Contract encompasses the Expiration Values that <candidate/party/option>

has won <election>. Specifically:
For direct democratic elections:
<candidate/party/option> is declared the winner by the relevant electoral authority and

either (i) is inaugurated/sworn in/takes office, or (ii) the scheduled inauguration date passes without a different candidate

taking office (delays in inauguration are considered for this purpose).
For parliamentary/legislative elections:
<candidate/party/option> wins the most seats in the specified chamber based on

final official results. In bicameral systems, this refers to the lower house unless otherwise specified. Overhang seats, leveling

seats, and appointed seats count only if specified. If two or more parties have the same number of seats, the party with the

higher share of the total vote will resolve to Yes and all others to No, unless the Exchange specifies at the time of listing that

such a tie will instead resolve in favor of the party entering government (in which case, if both or neither tied party enters

government, the party with the higher share of the vote will resolve to Yes and all others to No).
For religious elections:
The individual selected through the prescribed religious process (e.g., papal conclave reaching two-
thirds majority, Orthodox synod selection, Buddhist recognition process) and confirmed by the relevant religious authority.

For papal elections, white smoke and habemus papam announcement; for Orthodox patriarchs, enthronement; for other

positions, the equivalent ceremonial confirmation.
For traditional/customary leadership:
The individual selected through traditional processes AND formally recognized by

relevant governmental authorities where such recognition is required by law. If governmental recognition is not required,

selection through traditional processes alone suffices.
For judicial elections/retentions:
In partisan/nonpartisan elections, the candidate receiving the most votes; in retention

elections, "Yes" if the judge receives the required percentage (typically majority) to retain office; in merit selection systems,

the individual ultimately appointed following the prescribed process.
For recall elections:
"Yes" resolves if the official is recalled (typically requiring majority of votes cast); "No" resolves if the

recall fails or if turnout/signature requirements are not met.
For votes of no confidence:
The motion resolves to "Yes" if it receives the required votes under parliamentary rules (simple

majority unless otherwise specified, or constructive no confidence requiring alternative government proposal).
For referenda/plebiscites:
The specified option achieves the required threshold per applicable law (simple majority,

supermajority, dual majority, turnout requirements). If multiple thresholds exist (e.g., majority of votes AND majority of

states), all must be met. Failure to meet turnout requirements results in "No" unless the Exchange specifies a "Failed to meet

turnout" option.
For indirect elections:
<candidate/party/option> receives the required votes from the electoral body as certified by that

body's presiding authority. For multi-stage indirect elections (e.g., China's tiered system), the final stage determines the

outcome.
For professional/corporate elections:
The individual selected by the prescribed process (shareholder vote, board selection,

member bank election) and certified by the corporate secretary or equivalent authority.
For hereditary positions with electoral components:
The individual selected through the prescribed mixture of hereditary

succession and electoral confirmation (e.g., Malaysian King, UAE President).

[page 3 of 4: text layer]
For rotational/consensual systems:
The individual/party designated for the specified term according to the established

rotation or consensual allocation (e.g., Lebanese confessional system, Swiss Federal Council, Bosnian Presidency).
Special provisions:
Annulled elections:
If results are annulled by a court/authority AFTER announcement but BEFORE the winner takes

office, the Contract remains open until re-run election or expiration
Postponed elections:
Contract remains open until the rescheduled election or two years from the original date,

whichever comes first. Repeated postponements count towards the 2-year deadline.
Extra-constitutional interruptions:
Military coups, revolutions, or foreign interventions do not affect resolution if

the electoral process was completed and results announced by Source Agencies
Death/incapacitation:
If a winning candidate dies/is incapacitated after election but before taking office, that

candidate still resolves to Yes.
Ties:
If multiple candidates/parties tie, the Contract resolves Yes for whoever: (1) wins through the jurisdiction's

tiebreak mechanism, or (2) if no mechanism exists, received the largest share of total votes For

parliamentary/legislative elections, if multiple candidates/parties tie in the number of seats won, the Contract resolves

Yes for the candidate/party that received the largest share of total votes, notwithstanding clause (1) and without regard

to any subsequent government formation process, unless the Exchange specifies otherwise at the time of listing.
Information opacity:
For elections with extreme secrecy (religious conclaves, some traditional selections), resolution

depends on formal announcement by the designated authority, even if the selection process is not transparent
Disputed legitimacy:
In cases of competing claims (two presidents, disputed succession), the individual recognized by

the hierarchical majority of Source Agencies prevails
Write-in candidates:
Count only where legally valid and officially tallied
Partial elections:
Only seats/positions actually contested in the specified election count
Pre-selection vetting:
Candidates eliminated by vetting bodies before the election do not resolve to Yes regardless of

popular support
Examples that would resolve to Yes:
Candidate wins election and takes office normally
Party wins most parliamentary seats even if excluded from government
Cardinal elected Pope and accepts following white smoke
Traditional chief selected by elders and recognized by government
Judge retained with 55% approval in retention election
Referendum passes with required majority and turnout
Official recalled after successful recall petition and vote
Government falls after losing no-confidence vote
Examples that would NOT resolve to Yes:
Candidate leads polls but loses election
Party forms government but has fewer seats than another party
Cardinal reportedly favored in conclave but not elected
Traditional selection disputed and not recognized by government
Judge receives 45% in retention election (below majority threshold)
Referendum majority but fails turnout requirement (unless specified otherwise)
Recall petition qualifies but recall vote fails
No-confidence motion fails to reach required majority
Minimum Tick:
The Minimum Tick size for the Contract shall be $0.01.
Position Accountability Level:
The Position Accountability Level for the Contract shall be $25,000 per strike, per

Member.

[page 4 of 4: text layer]
Last Trading Date:
The Last Trading Date of the Contract will be the same as the Expiration Date. The Last Trading Time

will be the same as the Expiration time.
Settlement Date:
The Settlement Date of the Contract shall be no later than the day after the Expiration Date, unless the

Market Outcome is under review pursuant to Rule 7.1.
Expiration Date:
The latest Expiration Date of the Contract shall be one year after the scheduled date of <election>, or for

elections without fixed dates (religious, traditional, professional, confidence votes, recalls), one year after the triggering event

(death, petition qualification, motion filing). If an event described in the Payout Criterion occurs, expiration will be moved to

an earlier date and time in accordance with Rule 7.2.
For United States based elections, this Contract may be resolved on an accelerated basis if (A) at least four (4) of the eight

(8) Designated Media Sources have declared a winning candidate, party, or option, and (B) none of the Designated Media

Sources have issued a contradictory declaration. “Designated Media Sources” are: The New York Times (NYT), The

Associated Press (AP), Decision Desk HQ (DDHQ), CNN, Fox News, NBC News, CBS News, and ABC News. Should one

of the Designated Media Sources cease to provide independent election calls, it may be replaced at the sole discretion of the

Exchange. For the purposes of this clause, a source declares a winning candidate, party, or option when it makes either (i) a

formal projection of victory by its centralized decision desk, or (ii) an unambiguous statement in a news article that the

candidate/party/option has won. For the network sources (Fox, NBC, CBS, ABC), a declaration from a local affiliate may

represent the parent network; however, a declaration from the national desk shall always supersede any affiliate’s call. In all

instances, a parent network and all of its affiliates shall collectively constitute a single source for the purpose of this clause.
For international elections, this Contract may be resolved on an accelerated basis if at least two (2) of the six (6) Designated

International Media Sources have published an unambiguous statement that a candidate, party, or option has won. A

statement is considered unambiguous only if it conveys, in substance, that the candidate, party, or option has won or secured

victory; statements indicating that a candidate is “leading,” “on course to win,” “likely to win,” or similar conditional language

shall not qualify. “Designated International Media Sources” are: Reuters, The Associated Press (AP), Agence France-Presse

(AFP), BBC News, Bloomberg, and The New York Times (NYT). Should one of the Designated International Media Sources

cease independent international election reporting, it may be replaced at the sole discretion of the Exchange.
Expiration time:
The Expiration time of the Contract shall be 10:00 AM ET.
Settlement Value:
The Settlement Value for this Contract is $1.00.
Expiration Value:
The Expiration Value is the value of the Underlying as documented by the Source Agency on the

Expiration Date at the Expiration time.
Contingencies:
Before Settlement, Kalshi may, at its sole discretion, initiate the Market Outcome Review Process pursuant

to Rule 6.3(d) of the Rulebook. If an Expiration Value cannot be determined on the Expiration Date, Kalshi has the right to

determine payouts pursuant to Rule 6.3(b) in the Rulebook.

At.description: The condition holds at the instant `at` (spec §4).
At.title: At

By.description:
The condition holds at some observation up to the deadline, which is included or not as `closed` says (spec §4
"By(expr, t)"; A05 §5.4 endpoint inclusion). `since` is the earliest observation that counts, with its own
inclusion, or None where every earlier observation counts: the sources give By no lower bound, so the contract
states it (ours).
By.title: By

Category.description: A category or text value, compared as given.
Category.title: Category

Cmp.description:
observable op value, at the instant or day its enclosing temporal operator gives (spec §4). The value's type is
the observable's (`VALUE_KIND`); a numeric value is compared at the observable's declared precision (A09 §10.3).
Cmp.title: Cmp

Computed.description:
A number computed by a registered consequence node from numeric sub-expressions (spec §5: "The contract IR
compiles into the computation layer, so the settlement function and the hedge payoff are the same code"; I7: code
owns consequences). The node is pure and registered (spec §4 @node), so the same arithmetic settles, prices and
fuzzes; over interval inputs its value is the interval of its outputs.
Computed.title: Computed

ConflictPolicy.description:
How disagreeing sources are reconciled: a registered procedure and its parameters (A05 §5.4: "Use a registered
procedure ID plus parameters, or an explicit typed policy"). The two procedures registered so far are ours, the
two readings of spec §4's precedence list that an evaluator can apply deterministically: precedence_first_available,
the highest-ranked source in the procedure's precedence that has published settles; require_agreement, the sources
named in `sources` must agree, or the result is disputed. A contract whose rule is neither is not supported exactly
(A05 §5.5) until its procedure is registered here.
ConflictPolicy.title: ConflictPolicy

ContractIR.description: A contract in the IR (spec §4). Every observable the trigger or payout references is declared.
ContractIR.title: ContractIR

CountTrue.description:
The number of calendar days of `days` on which the condition holds, counted in the window's time zone (spec §4).
Its value over three-valued days is an interval [k, k + u] (A05 §5.3).
CountTrue.title: CountTrue

DurationIn.description:
The time within the window during which the condition holds, in `unit` (spec §4); an interval over unknowns, as
CountTrue's is. calendar_day counts calendar days of the window's time zone; elapsed_day counts 24-hour periods, so
a daylight-saving change does not change it (A05 §5.4: "Define ... day-count conventions").
DurationIn.title: DurationIn

Exclusion.description:
An exclusion clause. One that changes settlement is operative and names the IR or interpretive node that carries
it; a disclosure note is marked non-operative (A05 §5.4).
Exclusion.title: Exclusion

Interpretive.description:
A condition a resolver must judge from text (spec §4): a question template and its bindings, answered by decision
models and mapped to a truth by its answer's status (spec §6.3).
Interpretive.title: Interpretive

ListingBinding.description:
One per-market listing field of a series and the IR value it fills (ours; spec §9.3's per-market fields). `field`
is the market record's field, a dotted path into its objects where the value is nested (custom_strike.Option).
`node` and `slot` name the value it fills: a node's threshold (Cmp, NumCmp), the instant it reads (At, ValueAt), a
By's bounds (since, deadline), or a window's ends (Throughout, CountTrue, DurationIn); or, with no node, one of the
timing's dates (open, close, expiration, observation_cutoff). The field's value enters as it is, in the slot's type:
a threshold takes the number, text or date its comparison's value is, an instant slot an instant.
ListingBinding.title: ListingBinding

NumCmp.description:
A count or duration compared with a threshold, e.g. CountTrue(...) >= 20 (ours: spec §4 puts CountTrue and
DurationIn in the Expr union, and a trigger on them, such as spec §2.5's "how many days ... will station S record at
least X inches", compares their value).
NumCmp.title: NumCmp

Observable.description:
A quantity a contract settles on (spec §4).

revision_policy: which vintage settles (spec §4). "final" is a finite rule only with a declared resolution deadline
or a fallback (addendum A05 §5.4: "An unlimited `final` vintage is not a finite settlement rule unless 'final' has a
declared resolution deadline or fallback"): `final_deadline` is the instant by which the value must be final, and
`final_fallback` the vintage that settles if no final value is published by the settlement determination. unit and precision: what a numeric value is measured in and the precision at which it is published
(A05 §5.4 unit conversions; A09 §10.3 thresholds at declared precision).
Observable.title: Observable

Payout.description:
Per unit (spec §4). currency, and rounding to `rounding_quantum` by `rounding_mode`, are explicit (A05 §5.1,
§5.4: "Define ... rounding"). payment: paid once at settlement, or per
period of `periods`, each period's amount paid after its end (A05 §5.3: "A count paid once at expiry and a strip paid
periodically can have identical terminal amounts and very different liquidity consequences").
Payout.title: Payout

ReadValue.description:
A number a resolver reads from text, with its unit: a term an instrument sets (an alternative monthly wage, a
modified overtime threshold). Decision models answer it as a closed set of bands (spec §4: a question answered by a
distribution over a closed set), so its value is the interval of the band the resolved answer names, and unknown is
the whole range (A05 §5.3: a number left open by unknowns is an interval, never a guess). Each band is [low, high),
the last [low, high], so a value on a shared endpoint belongs to the band above it (A05 §5.4: "Define open/closed
interval endpoints"). Ours: spec §9.3's specimen tests a cost computed from such terms, and spec §4's Interpretive
yields only a truth.
ReadValue.title: ReadValue

Ref.description: A versioned reference to another record or policy (addendum §5.1 VersionedRef).
Ref.title: Ref

ResolutionProcedure.description:
How the contract resolves (spec §4, amended by A05 §5.2 and §5.4). on_unknown_at_expiry says what an unknown
trigger means at settlement without changing the trigger's truth (A05 §5.2). early_expiration: "when_true" when the
contract expires early once its trigger is true (spec §9.3: "early_close_condition"; the Western Grazers terms: "If
an event described in the Payout Criterion occurs, expiration will be moved to an earlier date and time in accordance
with Rule 7.2"). Its timing is what the contract states: "first_true" where the contract itself fixes the instant at
which the trigger is first true on the observations then published; "per_exchange_rule" where it defers to a rule
outside the IR's sources, named in early_expiration_rule, and then the outcome is determined once the trigger is
true while the early date stays unresolved, named, until that rule is supplied (A05 §5.2: "Unsupported procedure
details must be reported, not guessed"). An extension names its length and what happens if the trigger is still
unknown after it.
ResolutionProcedure.title: ResolutionProcedure

ScenarioExample.description:
A published example: a scenario that passed fuzzing, with the evaluator's outcome (spec §8.5, I8). `evaluation`
is the content hash of the ResolutionEvaluation that produced `expected`.
ScenarioExample.title: ScenarioExample

SettlementBinding.description:
What a market record's settlement value reports (ours; spec §9.3: "settled markets supplying known outcomes"):
the observable whose value the exchange settled on, and the market field (`at_field`) giving the instant that value
is for.
SettlementBinding.title: SettlementBinding

Source.description: A source of an observable's values, ranked by authority (spec §4: rank 1 is highest).
Source.title: Source

Throughout.description: The condition holds at every observation in the window (spec §4).
Throughout.title: Throughout

TimeWindow.description:
A window of time (spec §4), with each endpoint's inclusion stated (addendum A05 §5.4: "Define open/closed interval
endpoints, timezone"). `tz` is the IANA zone in which calendar days of the window are counted.
TimeWindow.title: TimeWindow

Timing.description:
The contract's dates (spec §4), with the cutoff for observations and the payment lag distinguished from the
settlement determination (A05 §5.3: event, publication, observation cutoff, settlement determination and payment
dates are different dates). Lags count calendar days or business days, in the time zone `tz` (A05 §5.4: "Define ...
timezone, day-count conventions"); a business-day lag skips weekends and the holidays of `holiday_calendar`, whose
one registered calendar is the United States federal holidays of 5 U.S.C. §6103 (ours: the calendar the contracts
we build settle against; another is registered here before a contract can use it, A05 §5.4 "Mechanical policies
must be executable").
Timing.title: Timing

ValueAt.description:
A numeric observable's value at an instant, selected by the contract's revision and conflict policies (spec §4
Observable; ours: a computed test reads published rates, such as a minimum wage in effect on a day).
ValueAt.title: ValueAt

VoidTransfer.description: What a void returns per unit (A05 §5.2: "A void result does not imply a particular refund").
VoidTransfer.title: VoidTransfer

schema.description:
contract_reader: a filed series read into the IR as an instrument family (core.ContractFamily's fields that are
the reader's): the support classification with its assumptions and unsupported terms (core.HarvestedContract), the
representative market's IR (its id and version are code's), the bindings that say which IR value each per-market
listing field fills (core.ListingBinding), and what a market record's settlement value reports
(core.SettlementBinding). Validated as the core family it drafts, so an answer the definition refuses is refused
here, with the definition's reasons.
schema.title: HarvestDraft

request.system:
You read a listed event contract series' filed terms into Requisite's contract IR, a formal representation that one evaluator settles in three-valued logic. A series is one set of filed terms listed as many markets that differ only in their listing fields (a strike, their times, the event). You read it as an instrument family: one representative market's IR, and bindings that say which IR value each per-market listing field fills, from which code gives every market its IR. Code validates and tests what you propose; you only propose.

You are given:
- series: the exchange's series record.
- filings: the filed documents' text as extracted from their PDFs (the contract terms, and the product certification where there is one), with anything that could not be read.
- representative_market: the listing fields of the market whose IR you write.
- markets: how many markets the series has, their tickers, and each listing field whose value varies across them, with its number of distinct values and its values at a few markets.
- listing_fields: the market fields a binding may read.
You are not shown how any market settled, nor any price. Your IRs are checked afterwards against how the settled markets settled.

Produce:
- support: "supported_exact" when the IR carries every operative term as filed; "supported_with_explicit_assumptions" when it carries them only under assumptions you list; "unsupported" when a term that decides settlement cannot be expressed, which you name in unsupported_terms. Never simplify a term silently: a term you could not carry exactly is an assumption or an unsupported term, stated in the filing's own words.
- ir: the representative market's contract in the IR, or null when unsupported. Code sets its id and version.
- bindings: for each listing field that varies across the markets and that the IR depends on, the IR value it fills: field, node, slot. A slot is a node's "threshold" (Cmp, NumCmp), the instant a node reads ("at": At, ValueAt), a By's "since" or "deadline", a window's "window_start" or "window_end" (Throughout, CountTrue, DurationIn), or, with node null, one of the timing's dates ("open", "close", "expiration", "observation_cutoff"). field is one of listing_fields, a dotted path where the value is nested (custom_strike.<key>). The field's value fills the slot exactly as listed, in the slot's type: a number fills a number threshold, a text a text threshold, a timestamp an instant. Write the representative IR with the representative market's own values in every bound slot; code checks that the bindings reproduce it from that market's record. No bindings when unsupported.
- settlement: what a market's settlement value reports. The exchange's record of a settled market states "the value that was considered for the settlement"; name the IR observable whose value that is, and the listing field giving the instant that value is for, the instant the IR reads it at. null where the settlement value is no observable of the IR (for instance, the outcome of a criterion a resolver judges from text), or when unsupported.

How to read the terms into the IR:
- Observables are the quantities the terms settle on (a published value, a status, a date), each with the sources the terms name, ranked as the terms rank them, its revision policy as the terms state it, and for a number its unit and published precision.
- The trigger is the payout criterion. Mechanical conditions (a value compared with a threshold, a count of days, a date before a deadline) are Cmp, NumCmp, By, At, Throughout, CountTrue or DurationIn over observables. Anything a resolver must judge from text (whether an instrument qualifies, whether its effect meets a description, whether it is in effect) is an Interpretive node: a question template name and its bindings, stating the condition in the filing's words. A number a resolver must read from text is a ReadValue with bands; a computation the terms define is a Computed node naming a consequence function and its inputs.
- The comparison, and whether its bound is included, come from the filed terms and the market's rules text, never from a field's name; a strike field supplies only the value.
- Every node has an id, unique in the contract, short and descriptive.
- Timing, the resolution procedure (source precedence, conflict rule, what an unknown at expiry means, early expiration and its timing, extensions, voids) and the payout follow the terms exactly. Where the terms defer to an exchange rule outside the filing, name the rule (early_expiration_rule) rather than inventing its content. Where a date depends on events (an expiration that is the sooner of when data is available and a latest date), state the date the IR takes as an assumption, quoting the term.
- Exclusions that change settlement are operative and name the node that carries them; disclosure notes are not.

Read the terms whole before writing anything. Where the terms are ambiguous, do not resolve the ambiguity in the IR: list it as an assumption with both readings.

Where carrying a term exactly needs a construct the IR does not have, never approximate it silently. Either list it as
an assumption, giving the filing's words and how the IR carries them instead, or, when it decides settlement and no
faithful carriage exists, name it as an unsupported term. Constructs the IR is known not to have:
- a condition quantified over documents ("any instrument that ...", "a qualifying action"), where the IR can only
  read one named instrument;
- a reading whose answer is a single value other than the top of its range (bands are [low, high));
- a date read from text and compared;
- a source hierarchy for the evidence behind an interpretive condition, as distinct from an observable's sources;
- an unknown-at-expiry outcome left to the exchange's discretion;
- a settlement or payment date stated as a deadline ("no later than");
- a known payment whose date is left to an exchange rule;
- a missing-data rule for a payout quantity;
- what a binary or capped payout pays per period;
- an early expiration when the outcome is decided either way (the IR expires early only when its trigger is true).
Where the IR requires a field the terms do not state (a void transfer with no void path, a rounding mode), give the
neutral value and list it as an assumption that the terms state no such rule.

assumptions: Payout Criterion: '<candidate/party/option> wins the most seats in the specified chamber based on final official results' (the 2026 Brazilian Chamber of Deputies). The IR carries it as a category observable, the party that won the most seats under the contract's rules, compared with the listed option (custom_strike.Option). It assumes the option's name as listed identifies the same party or federation that the Source Agencies name.

Tie rule. The three texts disagree. (a) The contract terms PDF says: 'If two or more parties have the same number of seats, the party with the higher share of the total vote will resolve to Yes and all others to No, unless the Exchange specifies at the time of listing that such a tie will instead resolve in favor of the party entering government', and the Ties special provision says the same: 'notwithstanding clause (1) and without regard to any subsequent government formation process, unless the Exchange specifies otherwise at the time of listing'. (b) The product certification's Appendix A and the market's rules_secondary say: 'If two parties have the same number of seats, the one entering government will resolve to Yes and all others to No; if both or neither enter government, the one with the higher share of the vote will resolve to Yes'. The rules_secondary can be read as the Exchange's specification at listing, in which case (b) governs, or as a summary of the filed terms, in which case (a) governs. The IR does not choose between them: the tie rule is folded into the observable's definition, and a seat tie leaves the reading open.

Coalitions: 'only those formally registered with electoral authorities before the nomination deadline count, not post-election governing arrangements.' Several listed options are, or belong to, registered federations (for example 'União Progressista' and 'PP' are both listed). The terms do not say whether seats are counted for a federation or for each member party. The IR counts seats for the listed option as named.

Accelerated resolution: 'this Contract may be resolved on an accelerated basis if at least two (2) of the six (6) Designated International Media Sources have published an unambiguous statement that a candidate, party, or option has won' (Reuters, AP, AFP, BBC News, Bloomberg, NYT; replaceable 'at the sole discretion of the Exchange'). The IR has no media-consensus rule. It takes the outcome to be the one the Source Agencies report, and carries the acceleration only as early expiration under Rule 7.2.

Early expiration: 'If an event described in the Payout Criterion occurs, expiration will be moved to an earlier date and time in accordance with Rule 7.2', and early_close_condition says 'This market will close and expire early if the election winner is officially declared or certified.' This expires every option's market early, whether it resolves Yes or No. The IR expires early only when its trigger is true (when_true, per_exchange_rule, Rule 7.2), so a market that resolves No is carried to the latest expiration date instead.

Expiration: 'The latest Expiration Date of the Contract shall be one year after the scheduled date of <election>', at 'Expiration time ... 10:00 AM ET'. The IR takes 2027-10-04T14:00:00Z, the listed expiration_time, as expiration and observation cutoff. The listed close_time, 2026-10-05T15:55:45Z, is taken as the trading close as listed.

Postponed elections: 'Contract remains open until the rescheduled election or two years from the original date, whichever comes first.' This can run past the one-year latest expiration. The IR keeps the one-year expiration and does not model a postponement.

Annulled elections: 'If results are annulled by a court/authority AFTER announcement but BEFORE the winner takes office, the Contract remains open until re-run election or expiration.' The IR carries this by reading the observable as of expiration (revision policy as_of_expiry), so an annulled result is not the value read.

Disputed legitimacy: 'the individual recognized by the hierarchical majority of Source Agencies prevails.' The IR uses precedence_first_available over the ranked Source Agency tiers, which is not a majority count within a tier.

Contingencies: 'If an Expiration Value cannot be determined on the Expiration Date, Kalshi has the right to determine payouts pursuant to Rule 6.3(b) in the Rulebook.' The unknown-at-expiry outcome is left to the exchange's discretion, which the IR cannot express. The IR carries 'void' with a void transfer of 'nothing' as neutral values. The terms state no void rule or refund.

Settlement Date: 'shall be no later than the day after the Expiration Date, unless the Market Outcome is under review pursuant to Rule 7.1.' This is a deadline, which the IR cannot express. The IR carries a settlement lag of 1 calendar day and a payment lag of 0.
Rounding: the terms state no rounding rule for the $1.00 Settlement Value. The IR uses a quantum of 0.01 with half_even as the neutral value.

exclusions.text: Ties: for parliamentary/legislative elections, a seat tie resolves Yes for the party with the largest share of total votes, unless the Exchange specifies otherwise at listing; the certification's Appendix A and rules_secondary instead resolve it for the party entering government, then by vote share.
Annulled elections: if results are annulled by a court/authority AFTER announcement but BEFORE the winner takes office, the Contract remains open until re-run election or expiration.
Partial elections: Only seats/positions actually contested in the specified election count.
Coalitions/alliances: only those formally registered with electoral authorities before the nomination deadline count, not post-election governing arrangements.
Pre-selection vetting: Candidates eliminated by vetting bodies before the election do not resolve to Yes regardless of popular support.
Write-in candidates: Count only where legally valid and officially tallied.
Extra-constitutional interruptions: Military coups, revolutions, or foreign interventions do not affect resolution if the electoral process was completed and results announced by Source Agencies.
Postponed elections: Contract remains open until the rescheduled election or two years from the original date, whichever comes first.
Death/incapacitation: If a winning candidate dies/is incapacitated after election but before taking office, that candidate still resolves to Yes (not applicable to a party-seat contest).

observables.description: The party, coalition or alliance (formally registered before the nomination deadline) that won the most seats in the Brazilian Chamber of Deputies in the 2026 election (4 October 2026), based on final official results, counting only seats actually contested. Write-ins count only where legally valid and officially tallied, and candidates eliminated by vetting do not count. A seat tie is broken by the contract's tie rule (vote share, or entering government; see assumptions).
observables.schedule: Election 2026-10-04; final official results as published

sources.name: Official electoral commission, constitutional court, or equivalent electoral authority of the relevant jurisdiction (Tribunal Superior Eleitoral, Brazil); formal proclamation by the head of state or government when constitutionally required

United Nations Electoral Assistance Division, Organization of American States, African Union, European Union Election Observation Missions, Commonwealth Secretariat, Carter Center, International IDEA, International Foundation for Electoral Systems

Major newspapers of record in the relevant jurisdiction in order of circulation, Reuters, Associated Press, Bloomberg News, Agence France-Presse, The New York Times, Financial Times, The Wall Street Journal, BBC, France24, Deutsche Welle, NHK World, Al Jazeera English, The Washington Post, Axios, Politico, Semafor, The Information, ABC, CBS, CNN, Fox News, MSNBC, NBC

resolution.early_expiration_rule: Kalshi Rulebook Rule 7.2 (expiration moved earlier when an event described in the Payout Criterion occurs; accelerated resolution when at least 2 of 6 Designated International Media Sources declare a winner)
